A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Daily Oracle study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of eight LLMs, including temporal accuracy, constrained retrieval, gold-article performance, and refusal analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains and extends the model evaluations and adds original human annotation results, refusal-controlled analyses, and forecasting-market experiments in Section 3.3 and Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly reports switching the generation pipeline from GPT-3.5/GPT-4 to GPT-4o-mini/GPT-4o for later questions. This is a limited model-component substitution: the four construction stages, article-selection scheme, seven filtering principles, and generation/evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix C adds actual closed-book evaluations on raw and filtered human-authored questions from five forecasting platforms. This introduces a substantially different question population beyond Daily Oracle's news-generated questions. Daily Oracle also extends through December rather than September 2024; its languages, news outlets, and TF/MC task types remain stable.

E2.justification: v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5 list the same eight evaluated LLM versions, and BM25 remains the retriever. GPT-3.5 remains excluded from constrained open-book evaluation. The market experiments reuse existing models; GPT-4o-family models serve question generation, while ForecastBench appears in the literature comparison rather than as an evaluated forecasting system.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a human evaluation design with four annotators rating 30 TF and 30 MC questions, balanced market evaluations containing 12,438 raw and 3,232 filtered questions, and additional accuracy calculations excluding refusals. The retained Daily Oracle evaluation grows from 29,988 to 31,510 questions and extends its observation window. These are substantial added evaluation protocols, while the original BM25 top-five retrieval and five-month smoothing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's closed-book refusal rates and temporal regressions, v2 tests whether degradation persists after excluding refusals across all three settings. It also adds human validation of filtering, category distributions over time, forecasting-market quality and distribution analyses, and a Mixtral case study showing responses under different information settings (Appendices A–C).

E5.justification: v2 introduces inter-rater reliability estimation using Fleiss' kappa across four independent annotators, reported separately for seven criteria and as an average in Table 4. Neither version reports repeated model-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests; the new statistical reporting is confined to annotation agreement.

E6.justification: Reported endpoint accuracy declines change from 20.14%/23.26% to 21.55%/11.33% for TF/MC, using September versus December 2024 endpoints, so these are extended-series results rather than same-setting gains. Table 3 also revises retained entries, such as GPT-4's 2023 MC accuracy from 56.40% to 56.36%. Substantial new results include 89.52% human–LLM criterion agreement, 85.00% acceptance agreement, refusal-excluded degradation, and volatile forecasting-market trends.

T1.justification: The accessible-article date-range definition and exponentially weighted temporal regression formulation are retained. Neither version presents theorem or proof contributions, and v2's added agreement metrics and empirical analyses introduce no new mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a continuously updated daily forecasting benchmark and persistent temporal degradation despite retrieval, motivating ongoing model updates. Revised headline percentages, expanded supporting experiments, and stronger descriptive wording do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of refusals as potentially alignment-related and indicative of insufficient actionable knowledge, while distinguishing them from degradation that remains after refusals are excluded. Appendix C develops explanations involving market-question quality, sparse early coverage, and changing source/category composition, and qualifies Daily Oracle as complementary to human-curated benchmarks rather than inherently superior in question quality.

D1.justification: v2 documents supplementary collection with Newspaper3k, the timing and roles of the generation-model switch, human annotation instructions, market-data selection and balancing, and budget-limited proprietary open-book evaluation endpoints. The exact forecasting-model versions, retrieval parameters, and full prompts were already supplied in v1 and are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds ForecastBench and materially expands positioning against forecasting-market benchmarks in Section 2 and Appendix C. The earlier argument that sustained degradation demonstrates a more challenging benchmark becomes a broader argument about longitudinal coverage, consistency, and confounding, supported by analyses of Halawi et al.'s data. Publication updates to existing references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: The five-section main narrative and most existing prose remain recognizable. v2 makes targeted revisions to contributions, related work, dataset analysis, discussion, and conclusion; adds a human-evaluation subsection and Impact Statement; and expands the appendices. The prompt appendix moves from C to D with its substantive text unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the main paper into two columns, rearranges the temporal-regression panels, and moves the construction diagram from main-text Figure 1 to appendix Figure 7. It adds the human-agreement table and new distribution, refusal-control, case-study, and market-comparison figures. These substantially alter both the visual organization and the evidence displayed.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked independent question-quality validation and evidence separating temporal degradation from increasing refusals. v2's human audit and refusal-excluded analyses address these important gaps, while the market comparisons strengthen the rationale for the benchmark's longitudinal design. The audit remains small with only fair average agreement, and the generator switch is not controlled experimentally, but the new validation and robustness evidence substantially improve the paper's overall evidential quality.
